prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) enforces permissives/interlocks, timestamps changes, presents scoped status, produces Bay Status Digest→Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing), which separates indications/communications-quality from evidence, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip. North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller control/interlock separate, non-substitutable scopes; north blocks unready closes. Boundaries assign devices/confirmations; shared equipment requires coordination. Breaker Control Unit executes permitted commands only under satisfied conditions; control failure cannot inhibit protection. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects feeders, produces Relay Diagnostic Note. North Protection Panel protects assigned north equipment; Transformer Protection Panel retains sequence-independent authority. Station Gateway carries authorized communications, produces Protocol Retry Summary. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) aligns event times, produces Clock Drift Snapshot→Sequence Event Archive (Orchard), authoritative evidence store. Engineering Workstation restricts/revision-controls approved search/filter/export/configuration/history, produces Settings Review Receipt. Maintenance Remote Terminal permits approved access without local authority. Station DC System powers automation/protection, produces retained Battery Load Test Record. Control Room Operator submits equipment/state/timing switching requests, verifies conditions, coordinates/suspends work, reviews events; assesses alarm priority/source/time/bay corroboration, new-versus-standing status, protection significance/condition/service impact; protection operations/unexplained states demand prompt investigation. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) plans/coordinatess bays, checks clearance/conflicts, produces Isolation Boundary Card, confirms handback. Substation Supervisor authorizes changes, resolves priorities/exceptional authority, escalates availability. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) develops settings, reviews coordination/event-times/diagnostics. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) verifies identity/conditions, performs authorized work, sends Breaker Inspection Tag(condition/time). Requirements: ordered sequences/hold-points/stop-conditions; local/interlock precedence; authorized available remote control; communications-loss stale displays/work-stop, verified recovery. Time never controls protection; preserve original source/order/time/quality, flag uncertainty/corrections. Authorized bounded queries/quality-preserving exports; distinguish conclusions. Auditable administration, scheduled retention/authorized holds, capacity/ingestion/recoverability checks, protected tested backups, post-handback review. Settings: documented coordinated revision, independent review/approval, model/firmware verification, approved window, installed comparison/testing/discrepancy-resolution. Work: authorization,

New part:
S151: The Control Room Operator acknowledges alarms only after reviewing the indication and retains awareness of any condition that remains unresolved.
S152: The Control Room Operator uses the acknowledgement slip to record the alarm response and any outstanding action.
S153: The operator checks available device status and sequence information without treating a cleared indication as proof that the underlying cause has been corrected.
S154: The Feeder Protection Relay indication is reviewed against the affected feeder status and any related protection operation.
S155: The Bay Automation Controller provides bay-level status indications that support the operator’s assessment of the alarm.
S156: Glasswing shall retain alarm state and event information for operator review after an indication has cleared.
S157: The Sequence Event Archive provides time-ordered evidence for later operational review.
S158: The North Protection Panel contains the protection equipment associated with feeder protection functions.
S159: The Control Room Operator uses indications from the North Protection Panel to assess feeder protection operations and related alarms.
S160: The Transformer Protection Panel is dedicated to protection functions associated with the power transformer rather than feeder protection.
S161: The Transformer Protection Panel provides local indication of transformer protection operation for assessment during an alarm response.
S162: The Control Room Operator considers the condition of the Station DC System when alarms or protection indications suggest a possible control-power concern.
S163: A breaker status discrepancy is treated as an abnormal condition until its cause and operational significance are understood.
S164: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized review of protection and event information, not as a substitute for immediate operational assessment.
S165: The Protection Relay Engineer supports investigation when relay indications, settings concerns, or event evidence require technical interpretation.
S166: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S167: The Substation Supervisor is consulted when the alarm response requires escalation beyond routine operator actions.
S168: The Control Room Operator produces the Clearance Handoff Memo when an unresolved alarm condition requires a formal handoff.
S169: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback before the associated state-change evidence is considered available for authorized engineering review.
S170: After handback, the Control Room Operator verifies that alarm status, equipment status, and recorded evidence are consistent before closing the response.
S171: The station communications design separates supervisory requests, bay-level execution, and protection action so loss of one layer does not silently substitute for another.
S172: Station Gateway brokers authorized station traffic across control-room and bay networks, applying configured protocol mappings, addressing, and access controls.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
